hero.headline: Trump says US will respond after Iran downs Apache helicopter
hero.teaser: President Trump attributed the downing of an AH-64 Apache helicopter to Iran and said the United States would respond.
hero.body:
President Trump blamed Iran for shooting down a US Army Apache helicopter near the Strait of Hormuz and promised a military response to the incident.

The AH-64 Apache attack helicopter crashed off the coast of Oman early Tuesday morning during a patrol operation, according to US Central Command. The two crew members aboard were rescued in an unprecedented operation using an unmanned drone boat after spending about two hours in the water.

Trump announced Iran's responsibility through a post on his Truth Social platform. "I have just been informed by our Great Military that last night the Iranians shot down one of our highly sophisticated Apache Helicopters while patrolling over the Strait of Hormuz," he wrote. He confirmed the pilots were safe and uninjured but stated that "the United States must, of necessity, respond to the attack."

The crash occurred as tensions in the Middle East remained high following an exchange of fire between Iran and Israel on Monday. That conflict marked the most serious escalation in the strained ceasefire since the broader Iran war began on February 28. Iranian state television reported that Israeli attacks killed at least two members of Iran's air defense units.

The wider conflict has disrupted global markets. Energy prices have risen worldwide, and the cost of basic goods including food has increased. The war began after the US and Israel launched strikes on Iran, but negotiations over a permanent ceasefire agreement have stalled since an initial truce was reached in April.

The unmanned rescue vessel, called a Corsair and measuring 24 feet long, located the two aviators in what military officials described as the first known drone rescue at sea by the US military. Captain Tim Hawkins of US Central Command confirmed the successful retrieval.

Military officials did not initially explain what caused the helicopter to crash, stating it remained under investigation. Apache helicopters have served as key assets for American forces enforcing a blockade on Iranian crude oil shipments and tankers. The US has used these aircraft to maintain pressure on Tehran in negotiations while also supporting allies like the United Arab Emirates in intercepting Iranian drones.

Trump had previously expressed optimism about negotiations with Iran, suggesting a deal could be reached within two or three days. "We're very close to having a very, very good, strong, powerful deal," he said before the helicopter incident. He acknowledged the US could conduct additional military operations but expressed concern about civilian casualties, saying "a lot of people are going to be killed" if bombing campaigns continued for weeks.

cards.headline: Social Security Trust Fund Projected to Run Dry in 2032
cards.body:
The Social Security trust fund that supports retirement benefits for roughly 68 million Americans is projected to be depleted in 2032, six years from now, according to a new report from the program's trustees. Without congressional action, beneficiaries could face an average reduction in payments of 22 percent once the fund runs out.

The updated projection accelerates the timeline for Social Security's financial shortfall, moving the depletion date closer than previous estimates. The trust fund relies on payroll tax revenue and accumulated reserves to pay out benefits. When the reserves are exhausted, the program will only be able to distribute what it collects in ongoing payroll taxes, forcing automatic cuts to monthly payments unless lawmakers intervene.

The program currently provides retirement, disability, and survivor benefits to tens of millions of Americans. The average cut of 22 percent would represent a significant reduction in income for retirees who depend on Social Security as a primary or sole source of support. The trustees' report puts the issue on a defined timeline, increasing pressure on Congress to address the funding gap through tax increases, benefit adjustments, or other reforms.

Social Security has faced long-term solvency concerns for years as the ratio of workers paying into the system relative to beneficiaries drawing from it has declined. The aging of the Baby Boom generation has accelerated the drain on the trust fund. Policymakers have debated various solutions, including raising the payroll tax cap, increasing the retirement age, or adjusting the formula used to calculate benefits.

The 2032 deadline gives Congress a six-year window to pass legislation that would prevent the automatic cuts. Previous efforts to reform Social Security have faced political resistance from both parties, with disagreements over whether to prioritize revenue increases or spending reductions. The new projection is expected to reignite debate over how to stabilize the program's finances while protecting benefits for current and future retirees.

cards.headline: Earthquake Traps People Under Rubble in Philippines
cards.teaser: The most powerful earthquake to hit the Philippines in 50 years has left many people feared trapped under collapsed structures.
cards.body:
A magnitude-7.8 earthquake struck the southern Philippines early Monday, killing at least 37 people and injuring hundreds. The quake hit about 20 kilometers off the coast of Sarangani province, collapsing buildings across the region. Tremors were felt strongly throughout Mindanao and as far away as Manado in Indonesia.

Authorities have warned people to avoid damaged buildings due to the risk of aftershocks. Rescue teams continue working to reach those trapped in the debris from collapsed structures.

cards.headline: Israeli Strikes Hit Tyre After Iranian Warning
cards.teaser: Israel launched air strikes on the Lebanese city of Tyre despite Iran warning it could resume hostilities if attacks on Hezbollah do not stop.
cards.body:
Israeli air strikes targeted the Lebanese city of Tyre on Monday, following Iran's warning that it would resume hostilities if attacks on Hezbollah continue. Despite the Iranian threat, Israel proceeded with the strikes.

Christian leaders in Tyre have called for rapid international intervention in response to the Israeli warning. The strikes underscore escalating tensions between Israel and Iran over the conflict involving Hezbollah in Lebanon.

cards.headline: Severe storms to bring heavy rain, hail and damaging winds to millions across central U.S.
cards.body:
More than 90 million people across multiple states are preparing for a significant multiday severe weather event expected to affect the central United States this week. The weather system is forecast to produce heavy rainfall, large hail, and damaging winds across a broad region stretching from the Plains through the Upper Midwest.

Forecasters are tracking the potential for strong tornadoes and large hail across portions of the central U.S., with more than 120 million people potentially affected by the storm system. The Plains and Midwest regions are expected to experience the most substantial impacts from the prolonged severe weather outbreak.

The multiday nature of this weather event increases the potential for widespread disruption across affected communities. The geographic scope of the storm system covers a significant portion of the country's midsection, creating challenges for multiple states that will need to maintain heightened weather awareness over an extended period. Residents in the projected path are being advised to monitor weather conditions closely and prepare for possible severe thunderstorms.

The combination of multiple severe weather hazards occurring over successive days creates compounding risks for the affected population. Forecasters emphasize the serious nature of the threat, though specific timing and exact locations remain subject to change as the weather system develops. Local authorities in threatened areas are likely coordinating emergency response preparations as the system approaches.

The central United States is currently vulnerable to the types of atmospheric conditions that generate destructive storms, making this event particularly significant. The scale of the population potentially affected underscores the importance of this weather event for a major portion of the country.

Residents in the storm's projected path should ensure they have multiple ways to receive weather warnings and understand their severe weather safety plans. Having a communication plan and knowing where to seek shelter are essential precautions as this multiday severe weather event unfolds. Communities across the Plains and Midwest should remain vigilant as conditions develop throughout the week.

The Weather Channel and other forecasting agencies continue monitoring the system closely. As is typical with severe weather forecasts, residents are encouraged to stay informed through local National Weather Service offices and trusted weather sources. The extended timeframe for this event means that preparedness and ongoing awareness will be critical for those in the affected regions throughout the forecast period.

cards.headline: May Inflation Data Expected to Show Rise Above 4 Percent
cards.teaser: Economists predict inflation accelerated in May, potentially topping 4 percent for the first time in three years.
cards.body:
The Consumer Price Index report releasing Wednesday morning is projected to show annual inflation exceeding 4 percent for the first time in three years, according to economist forecasts. Bond traders have positioned their portfolios in anticipation of this surge, which could shape Federal Reserve policy decisions going forward.

The potential inflation uptick comes as major central banks reassess their monetary policy approaches. The European Central Bank is preparing for an interest rate decision amid similar price pressures affecting large economies worldwide.

cards.headline: Six Countries Impose Sanctions on Israeli Settler Networks
cards.teaser: Britain, France, and four other nations coordinated sanctions aimed at disrupting financial flows supporting attacks on Palestinians in the West Bank.
cards.body:
Six countries announced sanctions targeting Israeli settler networks involved in violence against Palestinians in the West Bank. The British government coordinated the measures with France and other nations.

The sanctions aim to disrupt the financial networks that support attacks on Palestinians. The coordinated action represents a multilateral effort to address settler violence in the occupied territory.

cards.headline: Ukraine Reports Recapturing 370 Miles of Territory
cards.teaser: A top Ukrainian commander said the country has retaken more than 600 square kilometers of territory, while retired US generals assess Ukraine is winning the war.
cards.body:
Ukraine has recaptured more than 600 square kilometers of territory in 2026, according to the country's military chief. Retired US generals said Ukraine is winning the war with Russia, as the Ukrainian commander reported significant territorial gains.

The Ukrainian military chief said the country liberated nearly 100 square kilometers more than it lost in May alone. The assessment from retired US generals marks a notable evaluation of the trajectory of the conflict.

cards.headline: Man Arrested After Stabbing Attack in Belfast
cards.teaser: A 30-year-old Sudanese man was charged with attacking another man in an assault that was recorded and spread quickly online.
cards.body:
Police in Belfast arrested a 30-year-old Sudanese man on suspicion of attempted murder following a stabbing attack. The suspect was charged with having attacked another man in an assault that was recorded and spread quickly online.

Northern Ireland police appealed for calm after the attack. The incident sparked calls for anti-immigration protests in Northern Ireland.

cards.headline: Anthropic Releases AI Tool Previously Deemed Too Powerful
cards.teaser: Claude Fable 5, a version of the company's Claude Mythos program, has been released to the public after causing a stir among technology, finance, and government leaders.
cards.body:
Anthropic has released Claude Fable 5, a public version of its Claude Mythos AI program. The tool had previously generated concerns among leaders in technology, finance, and government sectors, with the company initially suggesting it was too powerful for public distribution.

The release represents a significant shift in Anthropic's strategy for deploying advanced AI capabilities. Claude Mythos had drawn considerable attention from multiple sectors before the company decided to make a version available to the public.

cards.headline: NASA Names Next Astronauts for Artemis Moon Program
cards.teaser: The space agency announced its next Artemis crew, though they will not be walking on the Moon or traveling near it.
cards.body:
NASA has selected four astronauts for its Artemis III mission: commander Randy Bresnik, pilot Luca Parmitano from the European Space Agency, and mission specialists Frank Rubio and Andre Douglas. The crew is scheduled to launch next year.

Despite being part of the Artemis program, which aims to return humans to the lunar surface, this particular crew will not travel to the Moon or venture near it as part of their assignment. Their role focuses on other critical aspects of the program's mission objectives.

cards.headline: NASA names four astronauts for Artemis III lunar training mission
cards.teaser: The space agency selected a crew of four for a training mission scheduled to launch next year ahead of planned moon landings.
cards.body:
NASA has selected four astronauts for the Artemis III lunar training mission. Commander Randy Bresnik of NASA will lead the crew, alongside European Space Agency pilot Luca Parmitano and NASA mission specialists Frank Rubio and Andre Douglas. The team is scheduled to launch next year.

This training mission is part of NASA's preparations for future lunar surface operations under the Artemis program, though the crew will not travel to the Moon or its vicinity. The mission represents a significant step as NASA works to return astronauts to the lunar surface for the first time in decades.

cards.headline: White House to close to press during UFC event unless organization grants access
cards.teaser: Reporters will be barred from the White House during an upcoming UFC fight on the grounds unless the organization provides credentials.
cards.body:
The White House will restrict reporter access during an upcoming UFC event on its grounds, making press participation dependent on whether the organization grants credentials. This arrangement transfers traditional White House press protocols to the private entity hosting the fight.

The event will trigger extensive road closures across Washington. A Trump-backed super PAC is organizing a fundraiser the day before the fight with $1 million ticket prices. Legal challenges have been filed against the event, with critics arguing it represents an improper use of White House facilities.

cards.headline: Debate emerges over new U.S. quarantine facility in Kenya for Ebola risk
cards.teaser: A new American facility in Kenya intended for quarantine of U.S. citizens at risk of Ebola has drawn criticism from Kenyans and some medical professionals.
cards.body:
The United States has established a quarantine facility in Kenya to house Americans potentially exposed to Ebola. The U.S. government supports the center, but it has sparked significant opposition within Kenya, with residents staging protests against its presence.

A man was shot dead by Kenyan police during demonstrations in Nanyuki, a city 120 miles from Nairobi, as anger over the facility mounted. Protest organizer Patrick Wahome confirmed the death resulted from a gunshot wound to the head. Medical professionals who responded to the 2014 Ebola outbreak have also criticized the facility's establishment.

cards.headline: Jury convicts Texas teenager Karmelo Anthony of murder in track meet stabbing
cards.teaser: A jury found Karmelo Anthony guilty of murder in the fatal stabbing of a Frisco student during a school track meet.
cards.body:
A Texas jury reached a verdict finding teenager Karmelo Anthony guilty of murder in the stabbing death of Austin Metcalf, a Frisco student killed during a track meet. The trial drew significant attention in the Dallas area, with live updates followed by local news outlets.

Teen eyewitnesses testified during the trial, describing the stabbing incident. One witness said the attack happened suddenly, stating the assailant just came out of nowhere during the track meet event.

cards.headline: Serena Williams wins on return to tennis after nearly four years away
cards.teaser: The tennis champion delivered a winning performance at Queen's Club in her first match after 1,375 days away from professional competition.
cards.body:
The 44-year-old Serena Williams made a triumphant comeback to professional tennis at Queen's Club, partnering with Victoria Mboko in doubles competition. The pair defeated third seeds Nicole Melichar-Martinez and Erin Routliffe 7-6 (2), 6-2 to advance to the quarter-finals.

Williams' return after 1,375 days away from the sport captivated the crowd at the traditionally reserved venue. Her stellar performance alongside Mboko demonstrated she remains capable of competing at the highest level of professional tennis.

cards.headline: World Cup debuts set for Uzbekistan, Jordan, Cape Verde and Curacao
cards.teaser: Four nations will make their first World Cup appearances while several others seek to advance past the group stage for the first time.
cards.body:
Uzbekistan, Jordan, Cape Verde and Curacao will make their World Cup debuts in the upcoming tournament. Meanwhile, Scotland, South Africa, Canada and New Zealand are among nations that have previously qualified for the World Cup but have never advanced beyond the group stage.

The expanded World Cup is drawing significant attention as it unfolds this week, though the tournament faces multiple challenges off the field. High ticket prices, travel restrictions, political tensions and other complications are affecting the fan experience and adding layers of complexity to what is shaping up to be one of the most contentious World Cups in history.

cards.headline: Stock Markets Fall as Tech Shares Decline and Oil Prices Drop
cards.teaser: The S&P 500 and Nasdaq declined as technology stocks sold off and oil prices fell after Israel and Iran agreed to halt strikes.
cards.body:
Stock markets in Asia and Europe fell on Monday following a sharp selloff in US technology stocks. Investors are concerned about the spending plans of companies leading the artificial intelligence boom. The S&P 500 and Nasdaq both declined, with semiconductor stocks experiencing particular weakness after recent strong performance.

Oil prices have remained volatile following renewed attacks between Iran and Israel. After initially rising due to Middle East tensions, crude prices fell below $90 per barrel when the two countries agreed to halt strikes, reducing concerns about a broader regional conflict and the potential closure of the Strait of Hormuz.

cards.headline: SpaceX IPO Demand Approaches Four Times Oversubscription
cards.teaser: Investor demand for SpaceX shares has reached nearly four times the number of shares available as the company prepares for its Nasdaq debut.
cards.body:
SpaceX's initial public offering has generated massive investor interest, with order books approaching four times oversubscription as the offering closes ahead of the Nasdaq debut. The company plans to sell 555.6 million shares at a $135 valuation, raising approximately $75 billion in what is being positioned as the largest stock market launch in history.

The strong demand reflects significant appetite for shares in the aerospace company. Up to a quarter of the shares are being reserved for individual investors rather than institutional funds and banks, a larger allocation than typically occurs in major IPOs. The high level of oversubscription means many investor orders will go unfilled, though it may drive up the initial trading price when SpaceX begins public trading on June 12.

cards.headline: May Inflation Data Expected to Show Rise Above 4 Percent
cards.teaser: Economists predict inflation accelerated in May, potentially topping 4 percent for the first time in three years.
cards.body:
The Consumer Price Index report releasing Wednesday morning is projected to show annual inflation exceeding 4 percent for the first time in three years, according to economist forecasts. Bond traders have positioned their portfolios in anticipation of this surge, which could shape Federal Reserve policy decisions going forward.

The potential inflation uptick comes as major central banks reassess their monetary policy approaches. The European Central Bank is preparing for an interest rate decision amid similar price pressures affecting large economies worldwide.

cards.headline: U.S. Exports Rose in April as War Boosted Oil Demand
cards.teaser: American exports increased in April, slightly outpacing import growth, as conflict with Iran drove higher demand for oil.
cards.body:
U.S. exports increased in April, according to Commerce Department data, with export growth outpacing import growth during the month. Higher oil demand from geopolitical tensions contributed to increased energy exports.

The rise in exports reflected broader shifts in global energy markets driven by ongoing conflicts affecting supply and demand dynamics.

cards.headline: Wealth Concentration Accelerates Among Billionaires
cards.teaser: The fortunes of the wealthiest individuals are growing faster than ever, with Elon Musk potentially approaching trillionaire status.
cards.body:
Billionaires are seeing their wealth increase at an accelerating rate, demonstrating the rapid concentration of assets at the top of the income distribution. Elon Musk's potential path to becoming a trillionaire illustrates the pace at which the largest fortunes are expanding.

The trend reflects broader patterns in wealth inequality, as the gap between the richest individuals and the rest of the population continues to widen. The concentration of wealth has implications for economic policy debates, including discussions about tax policy and wealth redistribution.

cards.headline: Apple Delays AI-Enhanced Siri Release in Europe Over Regulatory Dispute
cards.teaser: Apple has indefinitely postponed the launch of AI upgrades for Siri in Europe due to a regulatory disagreement.
cards.body:
Apple has indefinitely postponed the European launch of its revamped Siri AI, which integrates the company's new artificial intelligence tool, Apple Intelligence. The delay stems from an unresolved regulatory dispute between Apple and European authorities over compliance requirements.

The upgraded Siri, set for a fall release in other markets, will function more like advanced AI chatbots such as ChatGPT and Google Gemini rather than a traditional web-based search tool. European users will be unable to access these enhanced voice assistant capabilities due to the ongoing regulatory conflict.

hero.headline: Apple unveils major Siri overhaul with third-generation AI models
hero.body:
Apple announced a significant upgrade to Siri at its annual developer conference, integrating the voice assistant with Apple Intelligence and marking a major shift in the company's AI strategy. The redesigned Siri, rebranded as "Siri AI," will launch widely in the fall and represents a fundamental departure from the company's previous approach.

The new Siri will function more like ChatGPT or Google Gemini rather than a traditional web-based question-and-answer tool. Mike Rockwell, Apple's vice president of Siri engineering, demonstrated the assistant's capabilities during the keynote, showing how it can perform complex multi-step tasks within a single interface. In one demonstration, Rockwell asked Siri to identify a sunset beach photo, retrieve a friend's address from the contact list, and provide directions with a stop at the friend's house, all without switching between applications.

Apple's partnership with Google powers the new system, with Siri now leveraging Google's Gemini AI model through a billion-dollar deal. The assistant will have its own dedicated app and can access Apple's native ecosystem across mobile and desktop devices. The tool will initially support English only and handle tasks including proofreading, shopping, calendar management, and providing nutritional information through the camera.

The announcement comes after years of delays and consumer frustration. Apple postponed the original Siri update, first announced in 2024, as its AI development lagged competitors. The company previously faced legal consequences for its marketing claims, agreeing in May to pay 250 million dollars to settle a class-action lawsuit alleging false advertising of Siri's capabilities.

CEO Tim Cook, who is stepping down in the fall after 15 years leading the company, oversaw the keynote presentation. Craig Federighi, Apple's senior vice president of software engineering, acknowledged the company's slower pace in AI development compared to rivals. "Some appear to be racing forward, seemingly pursuing AI for the sake of AI, without clear regard for the people that it's ultimately meant to serve," Federighi said.

Beyond Siri, Apple announced expanded Apple Intelligence features across Safari, messaging, and the Home app. The company also introduced new camera and photo tools powered by AI that can create, alter, and enhance images, developed with Google.

Apple also revealed enhanced child safety features, introducing customizable restrictions on content, contacts, and app access. A new setup assistant helps parents control what their children can view and gradually expand permissions as they age. Additional safeguards include requiring parental permission before children browse new websites, monitoring messages for harmful content, and simplified screen time management. Apple partnered with the American Academy of Pediatrics for guidance on age-appropriate access limits.

cards.headline: NASA names Artemis III crew for 2027 moon mission
cards.teaser: NASA announced the astronaut crew for its Artemis III mission and laid out an accelerated timeline for returning humans to lunar orbit.
cards.body:
NASA has named the crew for its Artemis III mission, scheduled to launch in 2027. The four-person team includes NASA astronauts Randy Bresnik, Frank Rubio, and Andre Douglas, along with Luca Parmitano from the European Space Agency. During the mission, the crew will orbit Earth while practicing docking procedures with their Orion capsule and two lunar landers.

Artemis III represents a crucial step in NASA's broader effort to return humans to the moon. Rather than landing on the lunar surface, this mission will focus on testing and validating the systems and procedures needed for future moon landings, including the planned Artemis V mission.

cards.headline: Federal agencies ordered to patch VPN vulnerability within three days
cards.teaser: CISA gave US federal agencies a three-day deadline to fix a VPN security flaw actively exploited by a ransomware gang.
cards.body:
The Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency issued an emergency directive requiring federal agencies to patch a vulnerability in Check Point VPN products within 72 hours. Check Point confirmed that hackers exploited the bug to break into dozens of organizations, including multiple government entities.

A ransomware gang has been actively using the flaw to gain unauthorized access to networks. The tight three-day timeline reflects the severity of the threat and the active exploitation already underway.

cards.headline: Anthropic releases Claude Fable 5, its first public Mythos-class model
cards.teaser: Anthropic made its Mythos-class AI technology available to the public for the first time with Claude Fable 5.
cards.body:
Anthropic has released Claude Fable 5, the company's first publicly available Mythos-class model. According to Anthropic, Fable 5 is the most powerful model the company has made widely accessible. The model demonstrates exceptional performance in software engineering, knowledge work, and vision tasks, with its advantages over competitors becoming more pronounced on longer and more complex assignments.

The release includes built-in guardrails that prevent the model from responding to requests in high-risk areas such as cybersecurity and biology. This safety-focused approach allows Anthropic to expand public access to its most advanced capabilities while implementing protections against potential misuse.

cards.headline: Tech companies explore shift to cheaper AI models
cards.teaser: Industry executives are evaluating whether less expensive AI models can handle current workloads without sacrificing quality.
cards.body:
Technology companies are investigating whether cheaper AI models can handle their workloads without sacrificing quality. If companies can successfully shift tasks to less expensive models while maintaining performance standards, it would fundamentally transform the economics of artificial intelligence deployment.

Such a transition would significantly reduce the computational costs that currently burden AI operations at scale, lowering barriers to entry for AI services and potentially reshaping competition across the industry.

cards.headline: Screwworm detection raises questions about human risk
cards.teaser: Health officials are assessing the threat screwworms pose to humans after the parasites were detected in the US.
cards.body:
Screwworms, parasites that can burrow into living tissue including through the skull, have been found in the United States, prompting health officials to evaluate the risk to humans. Experts characterized the probability of human infection as low but acknowledged it is not zero. The parasites typically target livestock and wildlife but can infect people under certain conditions.

Screwworms lay eggs in open wounds, and the larvae then burrow into tissue to feed. The species was previously eradicated from the US through a decades-long program but has returned in limited detections. Health authorities are monitoring the situation to determine whether expanded control measures are necessary.

cards.headline: NASA delays Artemis timeline amid technical challenges
cards.teaser: NASA pushed back elements of its Artemis program timeline, citing technical hurdles and frigid weather testing requirements.
cards.body:
NASA has named the crew for the Artemis III mission, scheduled to launch in 2027. The all-male crew will test systems ahead of a planned Moon landing. This mission represents a key step in NASA's broader effort to return humans to the lunar surface.

The agency has adjusted its Artemis timeline due to technical obstacles and weather-related testing delays. While Artemis III will focus on testing systems rather than landing on the Moon, NASA aims to achieve a lunar landing with the Artemis V mission in 2028.

hero.headline: Serena Williams wins first match in comeback after four-year absence
hero.body:
Serena Williams returned to professional tennis after 1,375 days away, securing a doubles victory at Queen's Club in west London. The 44-year-old and partner Victoria Mboko defeated third seeds Nicole Melichar-Martinez and Erin Routliffe 7-6 (2), 6-2 to advance to the quarter-finals.

Williams' comeback marks her first competitive appearance since the US Open in 2022. She had previously described her departure from the sport as "evolving away" from tennis rather than a formal retirement, though she remained on the retired players' list until last year.

The American announced her return through a Nike video with the tagline "Guess everybody heard the news." In a statement, Williams explained her choice of venue, saying: "Queen's Club feels like the perfect place to begin this next chapter. Grass has given me some of the most meaningful moments of my career, and I'm excited to be back competing on one of the sport's most iconic stages."

Williams' return to the drug-testing pool last December signaled her intentions to compete again. She had trained in Florida in preparation for her comeback, with rising player Alycia Parks posting videos of their training sessions in March.

Mboko, a Canadian ranked number 9 in singles, expressed enthusiasm about partnering with Williams. "I'm very happy," Mboko said. "Me and Serena have stayed in touch, which is really, really nice, because I really look up to her. I think for me I want to let the moment be for her. I feel like if she's ready to come back on her own terms, then I feel like it's up to her to announce that."

The decision to begin with doubles allows Williams to ease back into competitive play while managing court time with her partner. Williams has the option to progress to singles in future events, though a potential Wimbledon appearance would require rapid preparation given the short grass-court season. Wimbledon begins three weeks after Queen's, leaving limited time for singles competition before the championships.

Williams is widely regarded as one of the greatest athletes of all time. Her 23 Grand Slam singles titles represent a women's open era record, and she holds 14 Grand Slam doubles titles alongside her sister Venus, who remains active on the tour at 45 years old. Williams is the only player to win the career Golden Slam in both singles and doubles.

The crowd at Queen's Club gave Williams an enthusiastic reception as she warmed up on the grass. Her victory demonstrates that she retains competitive ability despite the extended absence. Her presence adds a significant storyline to the current tennis season, as the women's tour has evolved during her time away, with new champions emerging and younger players establishing themselves.

cards.headline: Bengals restructure Joe Burrow contract to free up cap space
cards.teaser: Cincinnati has restructured the quarterback's deal to create $10 million in cap room for the upcoming season.
cards.body:
The Cincinnati Bengals have restructured quarterback Joe Burrow's contract, creating $10 million in additional salary cap space for the upcoming season.

The move provides the team with financial flexibility to address roster needs before play begins.

cards.headline: Teen Miles Russell qualifies for U.S. Open with Charlie Woods caddying
cards.teaser: The teenage golfer had Tiger Woods' son on his bag during a successful qualifying round for next week's championship.
cards.body:
Seventeen-year-old Miles Russell earned a spot in next week's U.S. Open at Shinnecock Hills after competing in Monday's sectional qualifying. The world's No. 10 amateur secured the fourth and final spot from the Florida qualifier, advancing through a playoff.

Charlie Woods, son of three-time U.S. Open champion Tiger Woods, caddied for Russell during the 36-hole qualifier. The two are close friends and commercial agent partners who will both play college golf at Florida State.

cards.headline: Wild sign Michael McCarron to six-year, $20 million extension
cards.teaser: Minnesota locked up the forward who joined the team in a midseason trade and produced immediately.
cards.body:
The Minnesota Wild signed forward Michael McCarron to a six-year, $20 million contract extension. McCarron arrived with the team via midseason trade and quickly made an impact with his play.

The deal secures McCarron's future with Minnesota and removes him from the free agent market as the offseason approaches.

cards.headline: FIFA revokes Iran fan ticket allocation for World Cup matches
cards.teaser: The governing body pulled tickets designated for Iranian supporters at all three of the team's group stage games in the United States.
cards.body:
FIFA has revoked the ticket allocation for Iran fans at the team's three World Cup group stage matches in the United States, according to Iran's national football federation. The federation announced the decision on Tuesday, just 48 hours before the tournament's opening ceremony.

The timing of the revocation comes as teams prepare for competition. Iran will play three matches on American soil during the group stage.

cards.headline: Victor Wembanyama condemns attacks on Spurs fans by Knicks supporters
cards.teaser: The Spurs star joined players from both teams in speaking out against videos showing physical assaults.
cards.body:
Victor Wembanyama joined players from both the San Antonio Spurs and New York Knicks in condemning videos that circulated on social media showing New York fans physically attacking Spurs supporters during a recent game.

The incidents drew swift criticism from members of both franchises, who spoke out against the violence and called for safer, more respectful fan behavior at NBA games.

cards.headline: Texas court schedules Brendan Sorsby NCAA trial for February
cards.teaser: The case involving the Texas Tech quarterback will go to trial two weeks after the national championship game.
cards.body:
A Texas court has scheduled the trial between Texas Tech quarterback Brendan Sorsby and the NCAA to begin in February, two weeks after the College Football Playoff National Championship concludes.

The trial timing ensures the proceedings will take place after the college football season ends. Sorsby continues to serve as Texas Tech's starting quarterback as the legal case moves through the court system.

hero.headline: Netflix Docuseries on Michael Jackson's 2005 Trial Draws 17 Million Views in Five Days
hero.body:
Netflix's docuseries examining Michael Jackson's 2005 criminal trial achieved significant viewership numbers in its initial release period, drawing 17.8 million views within five days of its June 3 premiere. The four-part series, titled Michael Jackson: The Trial, debuted at the top of the streaming platform's television rankings.

The documentary series compiles accounts from multiple perspectives related to Jackson's 2005 trial, in which he was accused of molesting 13-year-old Gavin Arvizo. Jackson was ultimately found not guilty on all ten counts. The series charts events leading up to and surrounding the trial, including Jackson's earlier admission during a Martin Bashir interview that he allowed Arvizo to sleep in his bed, which prompted a police investigation.

According to the source material, the series presents testimony and accounts that many viewers may already know from books, podcasts, and blogs over the past decades. However, the documentary distinguishes itself by presenting accounts from both sides of the case and featuring previously unheard recordings of Jackson from 2000 and 2001. While these recordings are not presented as definitive proof of wrongdoing, they are described as concerning in nature.

The series includes interviews with various individuals connected to Jackson and the Arvizo family. Christian Robinson, a videographer who worked with Jackson in the 2000s, shares observations about the family dynamics. Louise Palanker, described as a family friend, recalls a mother dealing with divorce and her son's cancer recovery. The documentary also features perspectives from Shmuley Boteach, a rabbi and former spiritual adviser to Jackson, who expresses concern about Jackson's behavior while maintaining his belief in Jackson's innocence regarding abuse allegations.

The series also addresses materials discovered at Jackson's Neverland Ranch during the police investigation. Vincent Amen, a former publicist for Jackson, recounts discovering items that he describes as "grooming materials." These discoveries are presented alongside the emotional reactions of investigators involved in the case.

The documentary concludes with discussion of "Leaving Neverland," the HBO and Channel 4 documentary released in 2019 that featured detailed testimonies from two men alleging childhood sexual abuse by Jackson. That documentary explored allegations from Wade Robson and James Safechuck regarding their experiences at Jackson's ranch.

The strong viewership figures reflect continued public interest in Jackson's legacy and the ongoing debates surrounding his life. Since his death in 2009, multiple documentaries and investigations have revisited allegations against him, contributing to broader cultural conversations about separating an artist's work from serious accusations made against them throughout his life.

cards.headline: Jack White Announces New Album Frozen Charlotte Through Presale on Website
cards.teaser: The musician has made his followup to No Name available for preorder without an official announcement.
cards.body:
Jack White has quietly put his new album, Frozen Charlotte, up for preorder on his website without making a formal announcement. The album serves as the followup to his album No Name, and is scheduled for release this summer.

Two different vinyl variants of the album are currently available for preorder on White's website. The preorder page confirms the album title and summer release window, though White has not issued a press release or social media announcement about the project.

cards.headline: Nicholas Galitzine to Play Supermodel Hoyt Richards in Gus Van Sant Film
cards.teaser: The actor will portray the fashion industry figure in a new project from the director.
cards.body:
Nicholas Galitzine has been cast as Hoyt Richards in an upcoming film directed by Gus Van Sant. Richards became known as the world's first male supermodel, working with major fashion houses including Versace, Ralph Lauren and Burberry during his career.

Richards, now 64, traveled internationally for photo shoots and runway shows during his modeling career. Van Sant has not released plot details for the film, though it will center on Richards' life and career in the fashion industry.

cards.headline: Bleecker Street and LD Entertainment Acquire Helen Mirren Thriller A Talent for Murder
cards.teaser: The film about novelist Patricia Highsmith will receive U.S. distribution from the two companies.
cards.body:
Bleecker Street Films and LD Entertainment have acquired U.S. distribution rights to A Talent For Murder, directed by Anton Corbijn. Helen Mirren stars as novelist Patricia Highsmith, known for writing The Talented Mr. Ripley.

Alden Ehrenreich, who recently won a Tony Award for Becky Shaw, appears in the thriller alongside Olivia Cooke. The film centers on Highsmith, who wrote psychological thrillers and crime fiction during her career. The two distribution companies will handle the film's theatrical and home release in the United States.

cards.headline: Paramount CEO Tells Lesley Stahl 60 Minutes Will Maintain Editorial Independence
cards.teaser: David Ellison made the assurance to the correspondent following recent producer departures from the newsmagazine.
cards.body:
Paramount CEO David Ellison told 60 Minutes correspondent Lesley Stahl that the newsmagazine will have editorial independence, according to three people familiar with the conversation. The assurance comes after the company recently removed the show's top producers from their positions.

The conversation represents an effort by Paramount leadership to address concerns about the program's editorial direction. 60 Minutes has been a fixture of CBS News programming for decades, and questions about its independence have emerged following recent personnel changes at the network.

cards.headline: Vans Releases New York Knicks Edition Slip-On Shoes for NBA Finals
cards.teaser: The sneaker brand has created a special version of its Classic Slip On featuring the team's colors.
cards.body:
Vans has released a New York Knicks-themed version of its Classic Slip On shoe as part of a special Game Day collection. The sneakers feature orange and blue coloring instead of the brand's signature black and white checkerboard pattern.

The release aligns with the Knicks' appearance in the NBA Finals. Vans, a California-based sneaker company, has created the shoes as team-themed merchandise during the championship series.

cards.headline: Paramount Hires Former Biden White House Official Shuwanza Goff for Government Affairs Role
cards.teaser: Goff will serve as the company's lead Democratic government affairs executive based in Washington.
cards.body:
Paramount has hired Shuwanza Goff as vice president of U.S. government affairs. Goff previously worked in the Biden administration and will be based in Washington, D.C., serving as the company's lead Democratic government affairs official.

The hiring comes as Paramount navigates a pending merger with Warner Bros. Discovery. A memo sent to staff on Tuesday announced Goff's appointment. She will handle the company's relationships with Democratic officials and lawmakers as the merger process continues.

hero.headline: Trump says US will respond after Iran downs Apache helicopter
hero.teaser: President Trump attributed the downing of an AH-64 Apache helicopter to Iran and said the United States would respond.
hero.body:
President Trump blamed Iran for shooting down a US Army Apache helicopter near the Strait of Hormuz and promised a military response to the incident.

The AH-64 Apache attack helicopter crashed off the coast of Oman early Tuesday morning during a patrol operation, according to US Central Command. The two crew members aboard were rescued in an unprecedented operation using an unmanned drone boat after spending about two hours in the water.

Trump announced Iran's responsibility through a post on his Truth Social platform. "I have just been informed by our Great Military that last night the Iranians shot down one of our highly sophisticated Apache Helicopters while patrolling over the Strait of Hormuz," he wrote. He confirmed the pilots were safe and uninjured but stated that "the United States must, of necessity, respond to the attack."

The crash occurred as tensions in the Middle East remained high following an exchange of fire between Iran and Israel on Monday. That conflict marked the most serious escalation in the strained ceasefire since the broader Iran war began on February 28. Iranian state television reported that Israeli attacks killed at least two members of Iran's air defense units.

The wider conflict has disrupted global markets. Energy prices have risen worldwide, and the cost of basic goods including food has increased. The war began after the US and Israel launched strikes on Iran, but negotiations over a permanent ceasefire agreement have stalled since an initial truce was reached in April.

The unmanned rescue vessel, called a Corsair and measuring 24 feet long, located the two aviators in what military officials described as the first known drone rescue at sea by the US military. Captain Tim Hawkins of US Central Command confirmed the successful retrieval.

Military officials did not initially explain what caused the helicopter to crash, stating it remained under investigation. Apache helicopters have served as key assets for American forces enforcing a blockade on Iranian crude oil shipments and tankers. The US has used these aircraft to maintain pressure on Tehran in negotiations while also supporting allies like the United Arab Emirates in intercepting Iranian drones.

Trump had previously expressed optimism about negotiations with Iran, suggesting a deal could be reached within two or three days. "We're very close to having a very, very good, strong, powerful deal," he said before the helicopter incident. He acknowledged the US could conduct additional military operations but expressed concern about civilian casualties, saying "a lot of people are going to be killed" if bombing campaigns continued for weeks.

cards.headline: House advances reconciliation bill for immigration enforcement funding in narrow vote
cards.teaser: The House passed a procedural rule to advance a budget reconciliation bill funding immigration enforcement by a 213-211 margin.
cards.body:
The House advanced a $70 billion immigration enforcement bill on Tuesday, passing a procedural rule by a 213-211 margin. The Secure America Act, which the Senate approved last week, allocates $38 billion to Immigration and Customs Enforcement, $26 billion to Customs and Border Protection, and $5 billion to the Department of Homeland Security through September 2029. The measure funds agencies leading President Trump's immigration crackdown.

The narrow vote reflects weeks of Republican delays over internal disputes. Speaker Mike Johnson secured passage without Democratic support, and the bill is expected to advance to a final House vote soon. Trump has indicated he will sign the legislation once it reaches his desk.

cards.headline: White House blocked alcohol study after years of international research
cards.teaser: The Trump administration declined to publish results from a multi-year study on alcohol consumption effects that involved researchers from the US, Canada, and the UK.
cards.body:
In 2022, the Biden administration launched a collaborative study examining the health effects of alcohol consumption, bringing together researchers from the United States, Canada, and the United Kingdom. The multi-year international research project proceeded for several years as planned.

The Trump administration subsequently blocked publication of the study's findings. Some observers suggested the decision to withhold results came in response to external pressure, though the administration did not publicly explain its reasoning for halting the release of the research.

cards.headline: House GOP campaign chair predicts Republican seat gains in November elections
cards.teaser: Rep. Richard Hudson said he expects Republicans will hold the House and add seats in the midterm elections.
cards.body:
Rep. Richard Hudson, chair of the House GOP campaign committee, expressed confidence Tuesday that Republicans will maintain control of the chamber in the upcoming midterm elections. Hudson went further, saying "I think we'll pick up seats" in November.

Hudson's optimistic outlook comes as Republicans currently hold the House majority heading into the election cycle.

cards.headline: Hunter Biden returns to social media with responses to Republican critics
cards.teaser: The president's son has attracted hundreds of thousands of followers with posts responding to critics and making self-deprecating remarks about his personal history.
cards.body:
Hunter Biden has returned to social media on platform X with a series of posts featuring crude responses to Republican critics and self-deprecating jokes about his personal struggles. His renewed online presence has quickly attracted hundreds of thousands of followers.

The president's son's social media activity has generated attention from both supporters and detractors as he re-establishes his public presence.

cards.headline: California congressman defends state ballot counting process with sports analogy
cards.teaser: Rep. Ted Lieu responded to Republican concerns about California election tallying by comparing it to scoring differences between halftime and the end of a game.
cards.body:
California Rep. Ted Lieu (D) on Tuesday criticized Republican concerns about his state's election process using a sports comparison. He asked people to listen to Steve Hilton, the Republican nominee for governor, who said officials have been vigilant with no cause for intervention.

Lieu's analogy addressed ongoing Republican scrutiny of California's ballot counting procedures. He compared shifting vote tallies during the counting process to how a game's score at halftime differs from the final result.

cards.headline: Trump and Maryland governor dispute pace of Jack Nicklaus golf course renovations
cards.teaser: President Trump and Gov. Moore are at odds over renovations to golf courses at Joint Base Andrews.
cards.body:
President Trump and Maryland Gov. Moore are in disagreement over the pace of a Jack Nicklaus golf course project at Joint Base Andrews. The president expressed frustration with the speed of renovations at the military installation.

The dispute represents another point of conflict between the president and the Maryland governor. Joint Base Andrews is a military facility that houses golf courses undergoing renovation work.
